title: New image of SN 1987A
caption: The supernova remnant SN 1987A, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: SN 1987A · constellation Dorado · about 170000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, and R. Kirshner (Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics and Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation) and P. Challis (Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A bright ring surrounds the remains of an exploded star at the center of this Hubble image, set against a backdrop of stars and wrapped in red clouds of gas. This is Supernova 1987A, and the ring is made of material the star threw off about 20 000 years before it exploded.

A supernova remnant is the expanding debris left behind when a massive star blows itself apart. The red color of the surrounding clouds traces the glow of hydrogen gas. Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 took the main image in January 2017, while the colors of the stars in front of and behind the supernova were added from observations with the older Wide Field Planetary Camera 2.

Since its launch in 1990, Hubble has returned to SN 1987A several times, watching its dust cloud expand. Those repeated visits have helped astronomers build a better understanding of these powerful explosions.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.40 x 2.63 arcminutes) and distance (170000 light years), the frame spans roughly 119 × 130 light-years. Its light set out about 170,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The central view comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, including a hydrogen-alpha filter, with star colors added from Wide Field Planetary Camera 2 data. The red clouds show glowing hydrogen, and the other color assignments aren't published.
understand.eye: Hubble's long exposures and sharp view reveal a ring and clouds far too small and faint for the eye to make out.

explore: SN 1987A lies about 170,000 light-years away in the direction of the constellation Dorado. The full picture combines blue, visible, hydrogen-alpha and near-infrared filters from two different Hubble cameras.
alt: A bright ring around a central exploded star, surrounded by red clouds of gas and a backdrop of stars.
